# Global mixed inverse-power energy is exactly the blocked entropy selector

This is a short identification, not a new centerpoint theorem. Let all
occupied fibers K_z have positive d-volume, put p=d+1, and use the
canonical convex hull C of their mixed support. For Y in that support set

    E(Y)=inf_a integral_S [1+a.(W-Y)]^(-p) dmu(W),

where the affine denominator is strictly positive on C. Parameters are
restricted to the actual relative affine span.

For a fixed occupied base b, let F be its minimal face in conv(P). The
full-support infimum equals the same infimum restricted to fibers over F.
The lower bound follows by dropping the positive off-face integrals. For
the upper bound add t times an exposing affine functional which vanishes
on F and is positive on all other occupied bases, then let t tend to
infinity. If F is proper, finite full-support attainment is impossible:
a finite parameter has strictly positive off-face integrals.

At Y in the relative interior of that face hull, the face parameter
domain is bounded. At every boundary parameter its denominator vanishes
on an actual positive fiber; the integral of its negative p-th power
is infinite, since p=d+1>=d. This is the cone-section divergence proved in
`candidate 5a3c8a5af6aaf266`,
Section 3. The Hessian is

    p(p+1) integral (W-Y)(W-Y)^T L^(-p-2) dmu,

positive definite on the relative span. Thus the face minimizer is unique,
attained and interior, and its equations are

    integral (W-Y)L^(-p-1)dmu=0,
    integral L^(-p-1)dmu=integral L^(-p)dmu=E(Y).           (1)

Let B(b) and pi_z be the attained finite-base entropy value and escort in
`candidate 2b7d1c7e003a98d0`,
Sections 1--3. Write g_z for the ordinary fiber centroids and put

    Y_b=(b,sum_z pi_z g_z).

Actual convex compatibility puts Y_b in int K_b. The base-only optimizing
denominator L_z=1+alpha.(z-b) satisfies (1) at Y_b: its continuous moment
condition is exactly the definition of Y_b. Therefore

    E(Y_b)=B(b).

Conversely testing this same base-only denominator at ANY (b,x) gives
E(b,x)<=B(b), since it is independent of x. Equality can hold only when
x=sum pi_z g_z: otherwise the continuous derivative of the tested
functional is nonzero and a small continuous-parameter variation decreases
it. The same variation is legal on the compact face hull, and an exposing
base parameter realizes its value as a full-support infimum. Hence

    max_(x in K_b) E(b,x)=B(b), uniquely at x=sum pi_z g_z. (2)

This argument includes boundary marks and avoids assuming smoothness of
the optimized value there. In particular the maximum over S is attained,
and its maximizing points are exactly the maximizing-base entropy marks.

The already certified actual counterexample is n=1,d=2, with

    T=conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)}, V=|T|,
    K_-1=T, K_0=3T, K_1=4T.

Their hull has exactly these integer fibers because (T+4T)/2 is contained
in 3T. The finite-base values are

    B(-1)=V, B(0)=153V/8, B(1)=16V.

All fiber centroids are zero, so the UNIQUE global-energy maximizer is
Y=(0,0). The actual containing closed cap x_1-8z>=0 has mass5V, whereas

    (Gamma_2/2)M=(2/9)(26V)=52V/9>5V.

See `candidate f3dc7a372eeb1eae`
for every cap and fiber calculation. Thus this exact global-energy
selector does not satisfy the requested OC bound. There is no new
arithmetic escape hidden in its full-space parameter: maximizing the
continuous mark forces that parameter's continuous component to zero.
